messages:
Christine Wong: Drafting status page update now. Current incident: increased streaming disconnects + elevated 5xx on /v1/chat/completions (stream=true). Trying to pick components + wording. Can someone sanity check before I hit publish?

Christine Wong: Proposed components: `Hosted API - Streaming (us-east)` + `Hosted API - API Gateway (us-east)` (unsure if gateway is actually impacted).

Christine Wong: Proposed copy (Investigating):
"We are investigating elevated errors for streaming chat completions in us-east. Some requests may disconnect mid-stream or return 5xx. Non-streaming requests appear unaffected. Next update in 30 minutes."

Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Sev1 declared by @Rafael Mendes. Incident INC-2417. Primary: Streaming disconnects (us-east). Zoom bridge posted in #eng-oncall.

Tomáš Novák: +1 on calling out streaming specifically. I’d avoid API Gateway unless we’re sure it’s gateway-level.

Tomáš Novák: Based on earlier guidance, if non-streaming works + embeddings ok, we should keep components tight. Otherwise customers see "API" and assume everything is down.

Aisha Bello: Looking at dashboards: error spike is mostly `stream_disconnect` + `upstream_reset` from streaming workers. Gateway 5xx is secondary (it’s passing through worker 5xx).

Aisha Bello: Non-streaming p95 latency + success rate are normal. Embeddings/rerank normal.

Rafael Mendes: Agree, do NOT tag API Gateway unless we have evidence gateway is failing independently.

Rafael Mendes: Component should be `Hosted API - Streaming (us-east)` only.

Christine Wong: Got it. So keep it to streaming component. What about the “chat completions” nuance? Some folks use stream=true on the chat endpoint.

Miles Thornton: We can mention the endpoint in text, but component = Streaming. That matches the new taxonomy intent.

Miles Thornton: Also: include customer action. Suggest retry w/ backoff or temporarily disable streaming if they can.

Sean Gallagher: Wording tweak: don’t say “appear unaffected” unless we’re confident. Say “At this time, we have not observed impact to non-streaming requests.”

Sean Gallagher: And give a concrete next update timestamp, not just “in 30 minutes” (customers ask “30 mins from when?”).

Amara Diallo: +1. Also avoid “disconnects mid-stream” w/out context. Suggest: “streaming responses may terminate early” (less scary but accurate).

Christine Wong: Updated draft (Investigating):
"We are investigating elevated errors for streaming chat/completions requests in the us-east region. Streaming responses may terminate early or return 5xx errors. At this time, we have not observed impact to non-streaming requests. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff or temporarily disable streaming if possible. Next update by 18:20 UTC."

Tomáš Novák: Looks good. Minor: “streaming chat/completions” reads weird. Maybe “chat completion requests with streaming enabled” or “/v1/chat/completions with stream=true”.

Aisha Bello: +1 to “stream=true” (that’s actionable).

Rafael Mendes: I’m good with either. Keep it short.

Christine Wong: Revised:
"We are investigating elevated errors for /v1/chat/completions requests with stream=true in the us-east region. Streaming responses may terminate early or return 5xx errors. At this time, we have not observed impact to non-streaming requests. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff or temporarily disable streaming if possible. Next update by 18:20 UTC."

Sean Gallagher: Ship it.

Christine Wong: Publishing now.

Incident Bot: Statuspage draft updated by @Christine Wong (INC-2417). State: Investigating. Components: Hosted API - Streaming (us-east). Next update: 18:20 UTC.

Christine Wong: Update posted.

Aisha Bello: Heads up, streaming error rate peaked ~12% and now down to ~6% after routing shift. Not stable yet.

Rafael Mendes: We should prep Identified text once we’re confident it’s the keepalive timeout regression.

Tomáš Novák: If we move to Identified, call out mitigation in progress + that some customers might see intermittent terminations.

Miles Thornton: FYI from runtime channel: suspect keepalive timeouts between gateway and streaming workers after recent config push.

Miles Thornton: Metrics snippet:
`stream_disconnect_rate{region="us-east"} 0.06` (was 0.12)
`worker_5xx{route="chat_completions_stream"} elevated`

Christine Wong: Ok, drafting “Identified” candidate (not posting yet):
"We’ve identified the cause as a keepalive timeout issue affecting streaming connections in us-east. We are rolling back the related configuration change and shifting traffic to healthy pools. Streaming requests may continue to see intermittent disconnects during mitigation. Next update by 18:40 UTC."

Sean Gallagher: That’s solid. Ensure we only say rollback if actually happening.

Rafael Mendes: Rollback is in progress (Connor coordinating). You can say “rolling back” now.

Amara Diallo: Maybe add: “new streaming connections should gradually improve” (sets expectation).

Christine Wong: Updated Identified draft:
"We’ve identified the cause as a keepalive timeout issue affecting streaming connections in us-east. We are rolling back a related configuration change and shifting traffic to healthy pools. New streaming connections should gradually improve; some requests may still see intermittent disconnects during mitigation. Next update by 18:40 UTC."

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: Post when ready.

Christine Wong: Posting Identified.

Incident Bot: Statuspage updated by @Christine Wong (INC-2417). State: Identified. Components: Hosted API - Streaming (us-east). Next update: 18:40 UTC.

Tomáš Novák: Nice. This is exactly the clearer impact wording support asked for.

Aisha Bello: Confirming improvement: disconnect rate now ~2.5% and falling. Latency steady.

Sean Gallagher: Once <1% for ~15m we can go Monitoring. Don’t rush.

Christine Wong: Ack. Will hold until we have stable window + rollback fully complete.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks all for fast review. Keeping thread open in case we need to adjust components if blast radius changes.
